Sampled top-k metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; good margins against random negatives therefore cannot establish reliable full-catalog top-ten ranking ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). A 2024 sequential-recommendation study finds aggregate metrics conceal head/mid/tail differences: random negative training favors head items, while popularity-based methods can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost ([Prakash et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276)). RecSys 2025 work evaluates sampling reliability through resolution, fidelity, robustness and recovery of model rankings ([sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). SASRec-specific evidence also links negative sampling to overconfidence and poor discrimination among highly ranked items ([gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192)). These findings motivate diagnostics; they do not establish the cause of Electronics failures.

Proposed bounded audit: freeze the model and a seeded panel of training prefixes with observed next-item targets. Compare equal-size, unique uniform, target-frequency-matched and text-similar candidate sets against exact target ranks computed by chunked catalog scoring. Derive frequency from training interactions and text similarity from available titles/descriptions, using local TF-IDF; mask prefix-seen items while retaining the target. Report score margins, sampled/full top-ten disagreement, full-rank percentiles and variation across repeated candidate draws, stratified by target frequency and prefix length with cell counts. Explicitly label targets used during optimization as fitted-target diagnostics, not generalization estimates. Verify routing and panel coverage separately for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl before reporting any four-category macro. Treat text-similar unobserved items as potentially relevant competitors, not confirmed negatives. Keep the pinned 200-user/category, 99-negative, seed-42 validation HR@10 evaluator and selection criterion unchanged.
